In the rest‐frame of the glass the light travels at the usual reduced speed  

u′ = c/n = 1/n  (we set c = 1).

The glass itself moves with speed v toward the observer (along the same direction as the light).  
To find the light’s speed u in the laboratory we must relativistically add the velocities:

u = (u′ + v) / (1 + u′v)
  = (1/n + v) / (1 + v/n).

Multiply numerator and denominator by n:

u = (1 + n v) / (n + v).

This expression is less than 1 for any physical v<1 and reduces to 1/n when v = 0, as required.

Hence the correct choice is

(D) (1 + n v) / (n + v)

Answer: D
